claim: Over every 10-year stretch starting in a January from 1934 to 2016 (83 windows), $7,500 of cash earning the 3-month T-bill rate lost purchasing power in 39 windows (47.0%) even with no tax, as inside a Roth IRA, and in 47 (56.6%) in a taxable account at a 22% federal rate. The tax shelter was worth a median $578.37 of purchasing power per decade (largest $1,874.21, for the window starting 1980): the median real end value was $7,644.89 sheltered versus $7,098.09 taxed. In the latest full window (2016-2026) both lost: $6,790.14 sheltered, $6,477.33 taxed. Year by year since 1934, T-bills beat inflation in 52 of 92 years before tax and 40 after a 22% tax. Cash parked in a Roth keeps its tax but not its purchasing power; the larger stake is the contribution room itself, which the data cannot price. History, not a forecast.

numbers.definition: Number of start years 1934..2016. Window model: $7,500 placed in January of start year Y earns, each month, TB3MS/100/12 (3-month T-bill rate, percent per year, monthly compounding), for 120 months (Jan Y .. Dec Y+9). Roth: no tax. Taxable: at the end of each calendar year, 22% of that year's interest is paid from the balance, i.e. balance *= 1 + 0.78*(G-1) where G is the product of the 12 monthly growth factors. Real end value = nominal end * CPIAUCNS(Jan Y) / CPIAUCNS(Jan Y+10). Start years 1934..2016 (83 windows).

assumptions: Cash earns the 3-month T-bill rate (a proxy for a high-yield savings account or money-market fund) in both places; typical bank savings rates have often been lower.
Federal marginal rate fixed at 22% for every year (today's bracket applied to history), tax paid each year from the balance; no state tax.
Roth case: the cash sits in a money-market or T-bill holding inside the Roth with no tax and no withdrawals; contributions (not earnings) can be withdrawn tax- and penalty-free at any time.
The 2026 Roth contribution limit is $7,500, so the whole amount fits in one year's contribution for an eligible worker.
Monthly compounding of the monthly-average T-bill rate (discount basis); real values deflated by CPI-U NSA January to January.

provisions.cite: IRS, Retirement topics - IRA contribution limits (2026 limit)
provisions.quote: For 2026, the total contributions you make each year to all of your traditional IRAs and Roth IRAs can't be more than: $7,500 ($8,600 if you're age 50 or older), or if less, your taxable compensation for the year

provisions.cite: IRS Publication 590-B, Are Distributions Taxable? (Roth IRA return of regular contributions)
provisions.quote: You don't include in your gross income qualified distributions or distributions that are a return of your regular contributions from your Roth IRA(s).
